title: The IRS publishes graduated 2025 rate tables, not a single rate on all taxable income
summary: The IRS publishes graduated 2025 rate tables, not a single rate on all taxable income.
body: The IRS page of federal income-tax rates and brackets for 2025 shows separate tables by filing status. For married filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse, the table is a schedule of rates on slices of taxable income, beginning at 10 percent. The source says: "Married filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse. Tax rate on taxable income: 10% from $0 to $23,850; 12% from $23,851 to $96,950; 22% from $96,951 to $206,700; 24% from $206,701 to $394,600; 32% from $394,601 to $501,050; 35% from $501,051 to $751,600; 37% from $751,601 and up." A graduated table means different slices of taxable income are taxed at different rates. The page is the rate schedule, not a statement of what a household actually pays after credits, and not a theory of who bears the economic burden of the tax.
